name: Dzùùngoo
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Solomiac, Paul 2014 (thesis 2007, Lyon 2). Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du Dzuungoo de Samogohiri. Koeppe. Lyon2 thesis server dead, PDF not found online

new_statements.quote: Comme la plupart des langues de la famille Niger Congo, le dzùùngoo est une langue tonale. Nous adopterons ici la définition d'une langue tonale qu'en donne Denis Creissels : "toute langue où une commutation phonologiquement limitée à la hauteur ou à la mélodie d'une syllabe unique est susceptible de constituer la seule trace d'une commutation entre deux unités significatives minimales dans une construction inchangée" (Creissels, 94, 175). [...] Le système tonal du dzùùngoo présente trois niveaux de hauteur tonale lexicalement significatifs que nous désignerons comme ton haut (H), ton moyen (M) et ton bas (B).
new_statements.translation: Like most languages of the Niger-Congo family, Dzùùngoo is a tone language. We adopt here Denis Creissels' definition of a tone language: 'any language in which a commutation phonologically limited to the pitch or melody of a single syllable can constitute the only trace of a commutation between two minimal meaningful units in an otherwise unchanged construction' (Creissels 1994: 175). [...] The tone system of Dzùùngoo presents three lexically significant levels of pitch, which we will call high tone (H), mid tone (M) and low tone (B).
new_statements.citation: Solomiac, Paul. 2007. Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du Dzùùngoo de Samogohiri. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (dir. Denis Creissels), NNT 2007LYO20060. Chapter 6 'Le système tonal'.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Dzùùngoo is described as a three-level tone language (H, M, L; TBU = mora; floating H; automatic downstep after L). The description contains no statement about word stress at all — neither a placement rule nor an explicit denial; the chapter on 'le mot phonologique' (ch. 5, not archived) is summarised by the reviewer as covering syllable combinations, reduplication, word length and vowel harmony only.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. One incidental use of 'accent'/'syllabe accentuée' on p. 89 (ch. 3) concerns the H-toned diminutive suffix -rɪ́ in a historical comparison with Jula diminutives, not a stress rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on nouns and verbs (citation forms and in the utterance); tone assignment discussed at word and phrase level; no stress domain stated.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes the Dzùùngoo of Samogohiri (Burkina Faso, near the Malian border), the main variety of ISO dnn / Glottolog dzuu1241 (Solomiac calls it 'dzùùngoo, appelé aussi samogho'). Not to be confused with Duungooma (duun1242, Mali) or the other Samogo languages (Bankagooma, Jowulu, Seenku, Kpeengo).

sources.note: Opens 'Comme la plupart des langues de la famille Niger Congo, le dzùùngoo est une langue tonale' (p. 147); three lexical tone levels H/M/B, floating H, automatic downstep, register-tier analysis; instrumental F0 traces. Nothing on word stress / accent d'intensité / prominence in the 55 pages (grep accent, accentu, intensité, proéminence, stress, prosod, suprasegment; only hits are 'tendance... accentuée' = marked tendency, p. 187).
Abstract: phoneme inventory (ch. 3), syllabic structure of the word (chs. 2, 4, 5), tonal structure (ch. 6); 'accessible: oui' but no URL; Lyon 2 server refused connections.

McPherson, Laura. 2017. Compte rendu: Paul Solomiac, Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du Dzùùngoo de Samogohiri (Mande Languages and Linguistics 10). Köln: Rüdiger Köppe, 2014, 314 p. Mandenkan 57. DOI 10.4000/mandenkan.1123.
sources.note: Review of the 2014 book (a shortened version of the thesis). Summarises ch. 5 'The phonological word' as syllable-type combinations, reduplication, word length, vowel harmony (no stress); ch. 6: 'Dzùùngoo is a three-tone language (L, M, H) with automatic downstep... The TBU is the mora' (para. 14). No mention of stress anywhere.
